practices.practice: Create one MongoClient at process startup and reuse it (singleton) rather than creating a client per request; tune the connection pool (maxPoolSize/minPoolSize) to your hosting model.
practices.prior_belief: Create a single MongoClient (pymongo.MongoClient) at application startup and reuse it for all requests (singleton), configure maxPoolSize (e.g. 100) and close it on shutdown rather than creating a client per request.

practices.practice: Read the cluster connection string from the environment or a secret store (do not commit secrets into repo files or logs); use a placeholder .env.example rather than real secrets in examples.
practices.prior_belief: Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or from Azure Key Vault; never write the actual secret into logs, repo files, or example .env files (use .env.example with a placeholder).
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB connection string best practices env var DOCUMENTDB_URI

practices.practice: Store production connection strings / credentials in Azure Key Vault (or use Microsoft Entra / managed identities / OIDC) and have the service retrieve them at runtime rather than baking plaintext credentials into config files.
practices.prior_belief: Store production credentials in Azure Key Vault and have the service fetch them at startup (or use an identity-based secret retrieval flow) instead of baking plaintext credentials into environment/config files.
practices.source_name: Migrate from Amazon DocumentDB to Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB Key Vault connection string store in Key Vault

practices.practice: Always use TLS for connections to Azure DocumentDB (tls=true) and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Always use TLS/SSL when connecting (tls=true) and reject invalid certificates (do not set tlsAllowInvalidCertificates) so credentials are never sent over plaintext.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID

practices.practice: Create indexes on fields used in aggregation $match or $group predicates in production workloads (index single fields when appropriate).
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes on every field used in aggregation $match or $group predicates in production workloads (e.g. index {diagnosis:1}, {age_band:1}, {gender:1}, {region:1} and compound indexes for common multi-field filters such as {region:1, age_band:1}).

practices.practice: When building compound indexes, order keys by query selectivity and sort usage following ESR (Equality → Sort → Range).
practices.prior_belief: When building compound indexes, order index keys by query selectivity and sort usage (e.g. index {region:1, age_band:1} if queries filter by region then age_band; put the most selective field first).

practices.practice: Use a TTL index on a Date field (e.g., expiresAt) with expireAfterSeconds=0 to implement absolute expiry of cached summary documents.
practices.prior_belief: Materialized summaries stored in an aggregations_cache collection should include a UTC timestamp field (e.g. expires_at) and a TTL index created as db.aggregations_cache.create_index({"expires_at": 1}, expireAfterSeconds=0) to auto-expire cached summaries.

practices.practice: When materializing expensive aggregations, upsert the summary document with an idempotent update (use updateOne(filter, {$set: ...}, upsert=True) or equivalent) so retries or restarts do not create duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Implement refresh/upsert operations as idempotent updates (use update_one(filter, {'$set': ...}, upsert=True)) so retries don’t create duplicate or inconsistent cache documents.
practices.source_name: Updating data in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

practices.practice: Wrap network and operation calls with retries using exponential backoff and jitter, and retry on transient errors (network errors, MongoNetworkError, socket timeouts, and 429 TooManyRequests) with a bounded max retry count.
practices.prior_belief: Wrap network/operation calls with exponential backoff + jitter and retry on transient errors (e.g. MongoNetworkError, socket timeouts, and 429/TooManyRequests from Cosmos), with a bounded max retry count.

practices.practice: For large or memory-heavy aggregation pipelines enable allowDiskUse (allowDiskUse=True) so the server can spill to disk as needed.
practices.prior_belief: For large or memory-heavy aggregation pipelines allow disk spill by enabling allowDiskUse=True in aggregate calls when supported (e.g. collection.aggregate(pipeline, allowDiskUse=True)).

practices.practice: Design aggregation pipelines to filter and project early (place $match early, then $project to remove unused fields) so subsequent heavy stages (group, facet, sort) operate on fewer documents.
practices.prior_belief: Design aggregation pipelines to filter and project early: move $match, then $project (to remove unused fields), then $sort/$group before heavy operations or $facet so the engine processes fewer docs (i.e. $match -> $project -> $group -> $facet when appropriate).
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB aggregation best practices $match early

practices.practice: Use explain('executionStats') on representative aggregation pipelines to confirm the plan uses IXSCAN rather than COLLSCAN and to inspect keysExamined / docsExamined ratios; include this in reviews/CI for critical queries.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain() (or the documentdb MCP explain tool) on representative aggregation pipelines to confirm index usage and to detect COLLSCANs; if explain shows COLLSCAN add or adjust indexes or change pipeline order to avoid full scans.

practices.practice: When seeding or bulk-loading data, use batched inserts (e.g., groups of 500–2000 documents) or bulkWrite to reduce overhead and RU charge compared to many single inserts.
practices.prior_belief: When seeding synthetic datasets or performing bulk loads, use batched insert_many operations (e.g. batches of 500–2000 documents) rather than single inserts to reduce overhead and RU charge.
practices.source_name: Optimize write performance / bulk writes (Azure DocumentDB guidance)
practices.how_found: bulk insert optimize Azure DocumentDB batched insert_many

practices.practice: Monitor RU/s consumption and throttling (429 responses); schedule heavy refreshes during off-peak times or temporarily increase throughput (or use autoscale) during materialization windows to avoid throttling.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor RU/s consumption and throttling (429 responses) and schedule heavy refreshes during off-peak times or temporarily increase throughput (or use autoscale) for materialization windows to avoid throttling and long-running queries.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB RU/s throttling 429 schedule heavy refresh

practices.practice: Protect the cluster with network-level controls (firewall IP rules, Private Link / private endpoints) so only backend services and trusted admin IPs can reach the Mongo endpoint.
practices.prior_belief: Protect the cluster with network-level controls (firewall IP rules, virtual network/private endpoint) so only the backend service and trusted admin IPs can reach the Mongo endpoint.
practices.source_name: Manage public access / Use Azure Private Link (Azure DocumentDB)

practices.practice: Use customer-managed keys (CMK) in Azure Key Vault for encryption at rest for regulated workloads, and grant the cluster a managed identity to access the key store.
practices.source_name: Configure customer-managed key (CMK) for data encryption at rest for an Azure DocumentDB cluster

practices.practice: Emit telemetry and enable diagnostics for aggregation performance: record aggregation duration, RU charge, documents examined/returned, and cache hit/miss so refresh frequency and indexes can be tuned from metrics and slow-query logs.
practices.prior_belief: Emit telemetry for aggregation performance: record aggregation duration, RU charge (if available), document counts in/out, and cache hit/miss so refresh frequency and indexes can be tuned from observed metrics.

practices.practice: Limit aggregation result sizes and use projection to return only required fields (pagination or trimmed summaries) to reduce network payload and client memory usage.
practices.prior_belief: Limit aggregation result sizes returned to callers (summaries or pagination) and use projection to only return required fields to reduce network payload and client memory usage.
practices.source_name: Aggregation examples and projection guidance (Azure DocumentDB)

practices.practice: Prefer pre-aggregating high-cost summaries (materialized cached documents) for faceted dashboards and refresh them on a schedule or on-change rather than running full aggregations on every HTTP request.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer pre-aggregating high-cost summaries (materialized cache docs) for faceted dashboards and refresh them on a schedule or on-change rather than running the full aggregation on every HTTP request.

practices.practice: When using vector search, store vectors in a dedicated numeric array field with consistent dimensionality and create a cosmosSearch vector index with explicit dimensions, similarity metric, and tuning parameters (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and validate nearest-neighbour queries at scale.
practices.prior_belief: If using vector search, store vectors in a dedicated field with consistent dimensionality, create the provider/engine-specific vector index with explicit dimension and metric, and test nearest-neighbour queries at scale; validate vector-index creation APIs for the Mongo API in your cluster before relying on it.

practices.practice: In serverless environments initialize the Mongo client outside the handler and use small pools (maxPoolSize ~3–5, minPoolSize 0, short maxIdleTimeMS) to avoid excessive connections per warm instance.
Stay well under the 16 MB BSON document limit: avoid embedding huge lists in a single cached document and split large fields into side collections or paginate large summaries.
practices.prior_belief: Guard against document-size limits when designing summaries: keep individual cached summary documents small (avoid embedding huge lists) and use paging or multiple documents if needed (MongoDB has a 16MB document limit).

practices.practice: Use the service's diagnostic settings and slow-query logs (ingested into Log Analytics) and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation for production clusters.

When running aggregation-based dashboards, verify plans and index coverage with explain and, if a pipeline is long-running, consider materializing intermediate results or using $out/$merge to write summaries.

practices.practice: For search over text fields prefer Azure DocumentDB's createSearchIndexes + $search (textSearch) rather than the community $text index for richer analyzers and scoring.
Use $facet to compute multiple parallel aggregations in a single pipeline for faceted dashboards, but ensure upstream filtering reduces the input set before the $facet stage.

When migrating from other MongoDB-compatible services, run a compatibility assessment and test queries and indexes on a staging cluster; store the new DocumentDB connection string in a secret store or use Microsoft Entra ID where possible.

practices.practice: Use $setOnInsert with upsert operations to set creation-time metadata only on insert, keeping updates idempotent.

When tuning vector indexes, prefer DiskANN on M30+ for large collections, HNSW up to tens of thousands of vectors, and IVF for small datasets; tune lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree/efSearch to trade recall vs latency.

practices.practice: Automate index lifecycle: inventory indexes, hide/validate an index before drop, and drop unused indexes to keep per-collection index budget manageable.

practices.practice: When relying on diagnostic TTL deletion semantics, remember expiry deletions are performed by a background sweeper (≈60s granularity) and TTL is not instantaneous; do not rely on TTL for tight security deadlines.
Use collection-level unique index on natural keys (e.g. patient_id) and upsert by that key during seed to get idempotent seeding behavior.

Use $search + cosmosSearch for hybrid (lexical + vector) retrieval and tune BM25, fuzzy options and analyzers when you need full-text features.

Use update_one with upsert and $setOnInsert for cache creation timestamps so refresh jobs can replace cache docs atomically and idempotently.
